meta.objective: Identify and demonstrate vulnerabilities leading to system compromise
meta.standards: PTES · OWASP Testing Guide v4 · MITRE ATT&CK aligned
meta.legal_note: This assessment was performed against an authorized target in a controlled environment. All activity was confined to the agreed scope.

executive_summary.introduction: Your Company was engaged to perform a black-box penetration test against the Example Target. This report presents the findings, impact and remediation guidance.
executive_summary.objective: Assess resilience against unauthorized attack and demonstrate whether an external attacker can achieve significant compromise.
executive_summary.summary_of_results: The test identified 1 Critical, 1 High and 1 Medium risk findings.
executive_summary.overall_risk_rationale: A combination of weak authentication and an injection vulnerability allows remote compromise of the application tier.
executive_summary.high_level_recommendation: Prioritize the Critical finding and enforce strong authentication controls across all services.

scope.in_scope_services: HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, any exposed application ports
scope.objective: Identify exploitable vulnerabilities and demonstrate impact
scope.constraints: No Denial-of-Service; activity confined to agreed target

methodology.activities: Host discovery, port scan, service enumeration

tools_used: nmap, burp suite, curl, hydra, searchsploit, standard Kali tooling.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Login Form
findings.cwe: CWE-89 — Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
findings.description: The login form concatenates user input into an SQL query without parameterization, allowing an attacker to bypass authentication or extract data.
findings.risk: Full authentication bypass and potential data exfiltration from the backend database.
findings.steps:
1. Navigate to /login.
2. Submit username: admin' OR '1'='1' --
3. Observe successful authentication bypass.
findings.evidence: HTTP 302 redirect to /dashboard with session cookie for admin user.
findings.recommendation:
• Use parameterized queries / prepared statements exclusively.
• Apply input validation and least-privilege database accounts.

findings.title: Weak Password Policy — No Account Lockout
findings.cwe: CWE-307 — Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
findings.description: No rate limiting or account lockout is enforced, allowing unlimited password guessing.
findings.risk: Credential stuffing and password spraying succeed against weak or reused passwords.
findings.evidence: Valid credentials recovered after < 5 minutes of dictionary attack.
findings.recommendation: Implement progressive delays, account lockout and MFA.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers
findings.description: Responses lack Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, HSTS and other recommended headers.
findings.risk: Increased exposure to clickjacking, XSS amplification and man-in-the-middle risks on first visit.
findings.evidence: None of the expected headers are present.
findings.recommendation: Add a comprehensive security-header set via the reverse proxy or application framework.

attack_narrative.description: Full TCP port scan and service identification.
SQL injection in the login form grants an administrative session.

business_impact.summary: Successful exploitation grants an attacker administrative access to the application and the ability to read or modify sensitive data.
business_impact.cia: Confidentiality — High · Integrity — High · Availability — Medium.

immediate: Fix the SQL injection with parameterized queries and rotate any exposed credentials.
Enable account lockout / rate limiting and enforce a strong password policy.
medium_term: Deploy MFA on all administrative interfaces.
Add security headers and enforce HTTPS with HSTS.
long_term: Embed security testing into the CI/CD pipeline.

secure_coding_guidelines: Validate all input at the server to prevent injection attacks.
Use prepared statements / parameterized queries for all database access.
Enforce strong password policy, account lockout and MFA.
Apply security headers and use TLS everywhere.
Keep components current and remove unused services.
